geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the end cantilever into a split-wing massing so the root gesture can open a clear public threshold while preserving the existing bent host ancestry.
Align the wing split to the plan direction that can create an access-facing void.
Increase separation enough to register as a usable public opening.
Preserve an anchored base so the mass remains one hierarchy rather than two disconnected pieces.
Keep the ground spine low and legible as threshold support.
Widen the base enough to read as active frontage rather than a cosmetic slit.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the cantilever-only end condition with a split-wing public-threshold composition so the frontage can open into a real void instead of remaining sealed.
Orient the split across the plan so the opening reads toward the frontage edge rather than along the depth of the mass.
Open a legible central gap large enough to read as public space, not a decorative crease.
Keep a ground anchor so the composition retains hierarchy and does not fragment into unrelated pieces.
Make the ground anchor low enough to preserve upper hierarchy while strengthening the active street threshold.
Give the ground element enough width to read as usable frontage and support programmatic presence at grade.

rationale: The four views show a single coherent massing family with acceptable continuity and a readable dominant bent volume, but the form is still essentially a compact stacked block with only a very weak ground response. The parcel is responded to in orientation, but not in a meaningful public-space figure: the blue frontage edge is not opened by a court, undercut, or seam, and the top view confirms the mass mostly occupies the parcel as a bounded object rather than organizing an active threshold. That makes it visually plausible as a compact object, but not yet as neighborhood living with the required active street edge and public void. The silhouette is coherent and not over-clipped, so repair integrity is decent, but the program relation fails because the mass behaves more like a generic sealed small pavilion than a street-facing neighborhood building. The references support a transferable move toward a carved court or split-wing/terrace strategy with an explicit access-side opening.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion/cultural than neighborhood living; use the spatial logic, not the specific roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and an elevated connector can create a clear public threshold while preserving a dominant mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; avoid copying the multi-building campus condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like low-rise masses can organize around a landscaped court and stepped edges to support neighborhood-scale publicness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the legible void and frontage response that make this precedent work.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved central void and overhanging upper mass can repair the street edge while keeping the ground plane active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more open and transparent than the candidate; the candidate remains too sealed.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated horizontal massing with a courtyard/atrium void and gentle roof modulation supports a mixed-use neighborhood brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not yet achieve the accessible connected-wing/public-core relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Connected wings, terrace-like section shifts, and a central open space can preserve hierarchy while giving the building a public core.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied from the visible four-view diagram, but the public-threshold logic is still too weak for program_fit_hard_pass.
The blue access edge is not semantically matched by an open side, court, or entry seam.
Do not read the stepped upper form as good_step_mass; it is too minor to count as a program-meaningful terrace section.
A graph correction should preserve the dominant bent mass but add a carved void or split public threshold.
